messages:
alex: Noticing multiple GPU nodes in eu-west-1 failing to register after today's AMI/kernel roll. Nodes are bootlooping and device plugin isn't coming up.

maria: Which nodepool? Any obvious kubelet or kernel errors?

alex: gpu-prod-pool-afe (spot-backed). Kubelet shows device plugin repeatedly restarting. dmesg has kernel module probe failures.

sam: Paste the dmesg tail and a `kubectl describe node` for one of the bad nodes.

alex: Pasting clipped logs: 
```
[  234.567890] nvidia: loading out-of-tree module taints kernel.
[  234.567893] nvidia: probe failed with error -22
[  234.567900] nvidia: GPU 0000:01:00.0: firmware not compatible
[  234.567910] device plugin: failed to register with kubelet: rpc error: code = Unavailable desc = transport is closing
```

alex: `kubectl describe node ip-10-0-12-34.eu-west-1.compute.internal` shows Allocatable `nvidia.com/gpu: 0` and many `Device plugin not ready` events.

dryan: (typo) ry an: I mean ryan: Firmware not compatible suggests kernel/driver ABI mismatch. We rolled kernel 5.15.0-89 -> 5.15.0-102 earlier today, right?

maria: Yes, and we also bumped GPU operator from v1.11.x -> v1.12.0 yesterday (device-plugin image updated). Could be a coincidence but likely interacting.

sam: My take: kernel advanced, AMI driver is older. Two remediation paths: roll back kernel or update driver on AMI. Spot pool makes immediate driver recompile riskier.

jen: @oncall please take lead. This impacts ~12 nodes in eu-west-1 and is causing scheduling pressure in other AZs.

oncall: Starting cordon/drain for affected nodes, adding taint to prevent new GPU pods. Will keep critical jobs on dedicated capacity if possible.

infra-bot: deploy-checklist: cordon/taint/drain applied to 12 nodes in eu-west-1 gpu-prod-pool-afe. Runbook: https://wiki.redwood/internal/infra/gpu-node-failure

ryan: We should evaluate capacity across regions before spilling. Routing to other regions will increase cost — eu-west reserved pools are near commit for Q2.

alex: Quick test: manually installed nvidia-driver 525.85 on an affected instance and rebooted. After reboot the probe succeeded and `nvidia-device-plugin` registered (`NVIDIA Kernel Module 525.85 loaded`).

sam: Good repro. So plan is to bake AMI with driver 525.85 matched to kernel 5.15.0-102 and stage to one nodepool. Also add driver/kernel validation gating to kernel rollouts.

jen: Action items:
- oncall: complete cordon/drain & maintain incident page (ETA 30m)
- infra: bake AMI with driver 525.85 for kernel 5.15.0-102 and stage to a canary nodepool
- devex: add autoscale preference to prefer dedicated cluster when eu-west GPU capacity < 10%
- eng: add alert for `firmware not compatible` and `nvidia: probe failed` patterns

oncall: Incident page created: https://status.redwood/incident/INC-2026-118 — updating.

maria: Check NCCL logs in affected jobs; found `NCCL WARN Net/Socket : Unable to reach peer` and `NCCL ERROR AllReduce failed` in jobs that spanned the affected nodes. Likely a symptom not root cause.

ryan: If we need to spin up dedicated flex GPUs to keep customer SLAs, coordinate with finance — it's a cost event.

sam: After AMI bake, do a canary: replace nodes in single AZ, run multi-GPU smoke test and a latency throughput regression. If green, finish rollout.

alex: I'll open a PR to pin device-plugin versions in our cluster bootstrapping and attach repro logs + dmesg. Also writing a short playbook for future kernel-driver rollouts.

maria: Also add a CI test that builds the kernel module for targeted driver versions on new AMI images and runs basic registration before marking AMI as production.

oncall: Cordon/drain completed for 12 nodes. Infra proceeding with AMI bake. Will post progress every 15m. :thumbsup:

infra-bot: incident INC-2026-118 severity=high assigned_to=oncall

alex: Follow-up: include automated compatibility matrix test (kernel vs driver vs device-plugin) in AMI pipeline, so we catch this earlier.
